recommended_base: Quay (brief: "pragmatic") — adopted at approximately one fifth its proposed scope, reduced to its L0/L1 capability core (quay-abi, quay-dyn, quay-onnx, quay-linalg) plus its dependency philosophy. Its L2-L5 (quay-frame, quay-model, quay-learn, quay-plot, quay-io, quay-python) are cut entirely.
rationale:
DECISION RULE APPLIED: an unrebutted fatal flaw in a design's FOUNDATION is disqualifying; an unrebutted fatal flaw in its PERIPHERY is a scope cut. I verified every load-bearing critique claim against primary sources before ruling.

WHY ROWAN IS DISQUALIFIED (foundation failure, verified). Rowan's M1+M2 — ten weeks, its two foundational packages, the thing everything else stands on — are duplicates of shipped code inside Rowan's own hard dependencies. Verified at https://hackage-content.haskell.org/package/dataframe-core-2.4.0.0/docs/DataFrame-Typed-Schema.html : dataframe-core 2.4.0.0 (uploaded 2026-08-14T06:17:58Z) already exposes DataFrame.Typed.{Schema,Types,Record,Generic,Freeze,Util}, and DataFrame.Typed.Schema already provides Schema as a type-level [(Symbol,Type)] list with Lookup/SafeLookup/HasName, RemoveColumn/SetColumnType/SubsetSchema/ExcludeSchema/RenameInSchema/RenameManyInSchema, Append/Snoc/Reverse/ColumnNames, AssertAbsent/AssertPresent/AssertAllPresent/AssertKeyTypesMatch/AssertDisjoint/AssertAllColumnsHaveType/AssertRealColumn/AllColumnsReal/AllDouble, StripAllMaybe/StripMaybeAt/ToMaybe/WrapMaybe/WrapMaybeColumns, SharedNames/UniqueLeft/CollidingColumns/InnerJoinSchema/LeftJoinSchema/RightJoinSchema/FullOuterJoinSchema, GroupKeyColumns, IsRealType/IsElem, and class KnownSchema with schemaEvidence :: [(Text, SomeTypeRep)]. Verified at https://hackage-content.haskell.org/package/dataframe-operations-2.4.0.0/docs/DataFrame-Typed-Expr.html : DataFrame.Typed.Expr already ships newtype TExpr (cols :: [(Symbol,Type)]) a = TExpr { unTExpr :: Expr a }, col @"salary", an IsLabel instance giving #salary, and an operator set STRICTLY RICHER than Rowan's sketch (it has separate nullable-aware families .+. vs .+ and .>. vs .> that Rowan lacks), plus sum/mean/median/count/countAll/minimum/maximum/collect and lift/lift2/nullLift/nullLift2/ifThenElse/lit/castExpr/over/asc/desc. Worse, Rowan's schema kind ([Field] with a separate Nullability kind) does not unify with the incumbent's ([(Symbol,Type)] with Maybe in the element type), so a Frame s cannot consume any of the eight DataFrame.Typed.* modules it duplicates. That is a competing typed API inside its own dependency cone — javelin's fragmentation outcome aimed at the upstream whose goodwill the plan depends on.

WHY CONFLUX IS DISQUALIFIED (foundation failure, verified). Its self-described "single most important adapter in the project" is written against an API that does not exist. Verified at https://hackage-content.haskell.org/package/dataframe-learn-2.4.1.0/docs/DataFrame-Model.html : the real class is `class Fit cfg input where { type ModelOf cfg input; type FrameReq cfg input :: FrameKind; fit :: cfg -> input -> FrameFor input -> FitResult (FrameFor input) (ModelOf cfg input) }` with `FrameFor (Expr a) = DataFrame`, `FrameFor (TExpr cols a) = TypedDataFrame cols`, `FitResult DataFrame model = model`, `FitResult (TypedDataFrame cols) model = Fitted cols model`, and `data FrameKind = AnyFrame | AllDoubleFrame`. Conflux's `fit :: Config m -> DataFrame -> Eff' m m` drops the target argument, erases the typed/untyped frame indexing, and discards FitResult's schema tagging — the wrapper is strictly LESS expressive than the thing it wraps. Its claimed-novel tuning layer is also a regression: verified at https://hackage-content.haskell.org/package/dataframe-learn-2.4.1.0/docs/DataFrame-ModelSelection.html , upstream already ships `gridSearch :: Int -> Int -> [c] -> (c -> DataFrame -> DataFrame -> Double) -> DataFrame -> GridSearchResult c`, fully polymorphic in the config type and type-safe because you enumerate real records; Conflux replaces [c] with a string-keyed Map Text ParamValue that fails at runtime. A typed toolkit shipping a less-typed API than the deliberately-untyped incumbent is self-refuting. And every Conflux contract abstracts over N=1 live implementation, which inverts the Tables.jl/ChainRulesCore/narwhals precedent the whole design rests on.

WHY QUAY WINS DESPITE THE LOWEST-BUT-STILL-HIGHEST SCORE (4/10). All four of its fatal flaws are peripheral or correctable:
(1) The zero-copy premise IS false — I verified at https://hackage-content.haskell.org/package/dataframe-core-2.4.0.0/docs/DataFrame-Internal-Column.html that the Column GADT is BoxedColumn (Data.Vector) | UnboxedColumn (Data.Vector.Unboxed, requires Unbox) | PackedText | MergedColumn, with NO Storable-backed constructor; Data.Vector.Unboxed is ByteArray#-backed, unpinned, GC-movable, and has no stable Ptr. But this kills a PERFORMANCE CLAIM, not the architecture. The fix is to state honestly that the frame-to-buffer seam is a copy — exactly the trade numpy<->pandas makes — and to delete the Borrowed constructor and the "zero copy to Python" headline. Optionally, contributing a Storable column upstream is the real fix, and that becomes a separate, owner-decided project.
(2) quay-model duplicates dataframe-learn's shipped ModelSelection. Correct — so quay-model is CUT and its one genuinely additive idea (Generic-derived hyperparameter reflection) becomes an upstream PR on top of the existing polymorphic gridSearch.
(3) Twelve packages in 26 weeks is Owl/HLearn/Breeze arithmetic. Correct — cut to four capability packages plus one umbrella.
(4) The 15-minute Windows cold-install promise is unreachable in a source-only ecosystem. Correct — the promise is DELETED and replaced with CI-enforced measured budgets that fail the build on regression, with no absolute number advertised.

What remains after those cuts is the only material in all three documents that delivers capability Haskell does not have at all, under a permissive license, on the owner's platform. Two of the four are verified-open niches: hs-onnxruntime-capi is AGPL-3.0-only and frozen at 0.1.0.0 since 2025-07-24 (verified on Hackage) while ONNX Runtime itself is MIT (spdx_id "MIT", verified via api.github.com/repos/microsoft/onnxruntime) and v1.29.0 published 2026-08-12 ships onnxruntime-win-x64-1.29.0.zip plus win-x64-gpu_cuda12/cuda13 variants — so "train anywhere, run in Haskell, on Windows, with GPU, under MIT" is a capability that literally cannot be obtained today. And inbound Arrow remains unimplemented in Haskell.

Quay's philosophy also survives its critique intact: bind-don't-reimplement; native dependencies loaded at RUNTIME and never linked at build time (the structural answer to Haskell having no wheel/conda layer, and the single most defensible engineering idea across all three documents — every critique flagged quay-dyn as salvageable); ship the contracts nobody owns; simple Haskell with no LinearTypes and no dependent-type bet. It is also the only one of the three that avoids BOTH classic Haskell-DS killers (no new numeric prelude, no bet on unshipped GHC features) without landing on the curation-layer failure that Conflux lands on or the Frames-repeat that Rowan lands on.

Finally, the Windows differentiator is REAL and unclaimed: I verified both DataHaskell/dataframe workflow files — .github/workflows/ci.yml is runs-on: ubuntu-latest with ghc ["9.6.7","9.8.4","9.10.3","9.12.2"], and haskell-ci.yml is runs-on: ubuntu-24.04 in container buildpack-deps:jammy with ghc 9.4.8-9.12.2. No Windows, no macOS, anywhere. That gap is the cheapest possible falsification test of the entire thesis and is therefore Phase 0.
grafted_ideas: FROM ROWAN - Phase/Role leakage typing (Split 'Train, Pipeline 'Fitted) so fit-on-test and transform-before-fit are TYPE ERRORS. This is the single genuinely novel idea in all three documents and no library in any language ships it. It is roughly one module. Deliver it as a PR against dataframe-learn's existing DataFrame.ModelSelection, NOT as a rival package.

FROM ROWAN - The golden type-error CI corpus as a build-failing gate: ~60 known-bad programs compiled via ghc as a subprocess, output normalized for paths/versions, byte-diffed against checked-in .golden files, with a hard budget (top-10 mistakes <=6 lines, offending symbol named on line 1) and features CUT when they miss it. Novel engineering practice for typed Haskell libraries. Apply it to dataframe-core's EXISTING assertion families rather than to a new schema layer.

FROM ROWAN - Upgrade dataframe-core's existing TypeError sites (AssertAbsent, AssertPresent, AssertKeyTypesMatch, AssertDisjoint, AssertRealColumn, InnerJoinSchema) to GHC.TypeError.Unsatisfiable (GHC proposal #433, base-4.19+/GHC 9.8+) with hand-written messages carrying available column names and a Levenshtein 'did you mean'. Highest value-per-line item in the entire corpus; requires no new package.

FROM ROWAN - Schema-directed ingestion returning a column-level structured diff (expected type / inferred type / row number / raw offending text) instead of silent coercion. Direct fix for dataframe issue #177 (Double silently read as Int). Implement against the EXISTING KnownSchema/schemaEvidence, not a new schema kind.

FROM ROWAN - Rule 0 hardened: the default install path has ZERO native dependencies, and every accelerated backend is a SEPARATE PACKAGE rather than a cabal flag, so the cabal solver never even considers it. Justified by the statistics -> dense-linear-algebra precedent.
FROM ROWAN - Runtime cpuid dispatch for any C kernels, never ox-arrays' -march=native, which bakes the build machine's ISA into a distributed artifact.

FROM ROWAN - Bind cblas.h/lapacke.h (the C headers OpenBLAS actually ships) rather than raw Fortran symbols, and never reuse hmatrix's build system. Avoids the name-mangling and symbol-drift class of bug that blas-ffi documents (it had to drop SCABS1/DCABS1 because OpenBLAS and ATLAS lack them).

FROM ROWAN - The deletability principle: every program using the new layer must have a mechanical de-typing to the plain upstream API, so users can bail out mid-pipeline. Frames had no exit; that is part of why it died.

FROM CONFLUX - Generic-derived hyperparameter reflection (params/setParams/defaults) shipped as an ADDITIVE PR that makes the existing type-safe gridSearch :: ... -> [c] -> ... enumerable, serializable and diffable. Keep the types, add the reflection. Explicitly do NOT replace [c] with a string-keyed ParamMap.

FROM CONFLUX - Donate Windows (and macOS) CI to the dataframe monorepo as the FIRST deliverable, before any library code. Verified absent from both ci.yml and haskell-ci.yml. It is simultaneously the highest value-per-hour contribution available and the cheapest falsification test of the Windows thesis.

FROM CONFLUX - Time-to-first-result and cold-install wall clock as CI-enforced, BUILD-FAILING budgets with a >20% regression gate. Julia's TTFX history justifies treating first-run latency as P0. Publish the measured numbers; never advertise an absolute promise.

FROM CONFLUX - Help cut an IHaskell Hackage release carrying PR #1595's Windows support (ihaskell-0.13.0.0 from 2025-11-15 is bounded ghc <9.13 and predates it), plus prebuilt kernel bundles. Pure upstream work, and the single highest-leverage unblock in the whole onboarding chain.

FROM CONFLUX - The upstream-interaction rule: every contribution arrives as a FINISHED, TESTED PR that closes an issue the maintainer already filed (dataframe #181/#152/#177/#191/#192/#115, massiv #146), never as a design discussion. Correct model for 1-2 part-timers in a ~110-person ecosystem, and it protects the exhausted maintainers whose capacity the plan depends on.

FROM CONFLUX - Governance as a deliverable: two named maintainers per package before any 1.0, an explicit stable/unstable API split at 1.0 (Polars' 2024-07-01 precedent), and a written 'never fork what we can patch' rule.

FROM CONFLUX - Depend on granular subpackages (dataframe-core, dataframe-operations) with tight >=x.y && <x.(y+1) bounds, never the umbrella dataframe package. Justified by 68 published versions and 1.0.0.0 (2026-03-22) -> 3.5.0.0 (2026-08-14).
FROM CONFLUX - A machine-readable per-package platform-support table rendered in the docs, so no signature ever implies a capability the default build lacks on the user's OS.

FROM QUAY (KEPT, CORRECTED) - The precise ABI ownership discipline: imported structs become ForeignPtr with the C release callback installed as the finalizer; exported structs get a release callback built with foreign import ccall "wrapper" freeing a StablePtr keep-alive; bracket covers the borrow case. Enforced by pyarrow round-trip fuzzing, +RTS -s leak assertions, and valgrind on the Linux lane.

FROM QUAY (KEPT) - Hand-written Storable instances for the frozen C structs so the shipped library has NO cbits and needs no C toolchain, with a TEST-SUITE-ONLY C file of _Static_assert(offsetof(...)) checks that fails CI if any layout drifts.

FROM QUAY (KEPT) - `doctor` capability diagnostics: print exactly which native capabilities resolved, which did not, and the one command that fixes each. Applied to the existing ecosystem too (does your hmatrix see OpenBLAS? which MSYS2 environment are you in?), this is a cheap contribution to the ecosystem's #1 documented friction point.

CORRECTION TO QUAY (MANDATORY) - Kill the pure-gemm-over-mutable-global-backend design. unsafePerformIO over an IORef that withBackend mutates is not referentially transparent under laziness, and OpenBLAS vs a reference implementation differ in rounding, so the same expression can yield different values depending on evaluation order. Either the backend is pinned IMMUTABLY at init with no withBackend, or every backend-consulting operation lives in IO.

CORRECTION TO QUAY (MANDATORY) - Kill the blanket 'nothing ever hard-fails' claim. Quay's fallback covered gemm/potrf/gesv/gels only, leaving gesdd (PCA) and syevd (eigendecomposition) to hard-fail under a banner promising they could not. Either every exposed driver has a pure-Haskell fallback, or drivers without one are documented per-driver as requiring a backend.
unified_architecture:
NAME/POSITIONING: a NATIVE-CAPABILITY AND INTEROP FLOOR for Haskell data science — explicitly NOT a toolkit that competes with dataframe. The README's first sentence must be "this is not a new dataframe". The project's entire claim is that it adds capability Haskell does not have, and adds it on Windows, under a permissive license, without a build-time C dependency.

FOUNDING PREMISE, STATED HONESTLY: the pandas/scikit-learn/plotting tiers of the brief are ALREADY OCCUPIED and are shipping weekly (dataframe 3.5.0.0, dataframe-core 2.4.0.0, dataframe-operations 2.4.0.0, dataframe-learn 2.4.1.0, dataframe-viz 1.3.1.0, all uploaded 2026-08-14). What is missing is the layer BELOW them (BLAS/LAPACK that installs, ONNX inference, runtime native-dependency loading) and the layer BESIDE them (Arrow/DLPack interop, Windows CI, type-error quality, leakage typing). HSDS occupies exactly those two layers and nothing else.

DATA MODEL, STATED ONCE. The incumbent's DataFrame / Column / Expr / TExpr are the tabular and expression vocabulary — unchanged, not wrapped, not re-declared, not competed with. HSDS's own vocabulary is exactly two things: (a) a Data.Vector.Storable buffer plus shape/strides metadata, used for BLAS, ONNX and DLPack; (b) two frozen C ABI structs (Arrow C Data/Stream, DLPack). The seam between (a) and the incumbent's Column is an EXPLICIT, DOCUMENTED COPY, because Column has no Storable constructor — verified: the GADT is BoxedColumn (Data.Vector) | UnboxedColumn (Data.Vector.Unboxed) | PackedText | MergedColumn, and Data.Vector.Unboxed is unpinned ByteArray#-backed with no stable Ptr. This is the same trade numpy<->pandas makes and it must be stated in the API (a copy is returned, not a Borrowed/Copied tag pretending both are reachable).

=== TIER A: THE CAPABILITY FLOOR (net-new, no incumbent, four packages) ===
Each ships alone, is independently valuable, and leaves the ecosystem better off even if the project stops immediately after it.

A1. hsds-dyn — THE KEYSTONE. Cross-platform runtime shared-library loading, ~300 LOC. LoadLibraryW/GetProcAddress with AddDllDirectory called BEFORE load on Windows (OpenBLAS drags libgcc_s/libgomp; ONNX Runtime drags its own providers); System.Posix.DynamicLinker elsewhere. A documented search-path policy (env-var override -> per-user data dir -> system path). A Capability record = resolved FunPtrs obtained through foreign import ccall "dynamic" wrappers, plus a version tag, plus per-symbol lazy resolution so a missing symbol degrades ONE operation rather than the whole library. This package is the reason nothing downstream has a build-time native dependency, and it is the structural answer to Haskell having no wheel/conda equivalent. It is useful to hmatrix, duckdb-ffi, IHaskell's zeromq/cairo binding, and any future native binding, independent of HSDS.

A2. hsds-abi — Arrow C Data Interface + Arrow C Stream Interface (BOTH directions; inbound is the verified ecosystem gap — dataframe-arrow is export-to-Python only, harrow died at 1 commit, hs-arrow at 6 and is LGPL, and Haskell is absent from Arrow's official implementation list) and DLPack DLManagedTensorVersioned import/export. Hand-written Storable instances for the frozen structs so the SHIPPED library has no cbits and needs no C toolchain; a test-suite-only C file of _Static_assert(offsetof(...)) checks proves the layouts in CI and fails the build on drift. Ownership: imported -> ForeignPtr with the C release callback as finalizer; exported -> release callback via foreign import ccall "wrapper" freeing a StablePtr keep-alive; bracket for borrow. Conformance tested against pyarrow in both directions in CI on all three OSes, with leak assertions under +RTS -s and valgrind on the Linux lane. The inbound half is offered upstream to dataframe-core as a PR as soon as it works.

A3. hsds-onnx — THE HEADLINE CAPABILITY. MIT-licensed ONNX Runtime inference bindings resolved at runtime through OrtGetApiBase() returning a struct of function pointers (the C API is DESIGNED for this loading pattern). Env/Session/SessionOptions/RunOptions/MemoryInfo lifecycle under bracket; OrtValue <-> Storable buffer zero-copy in both directions via CreateTensorWithDataAsOrtValue; shape and dtype introspection; a graceful Maybe when the runtime is absent. Verified niche: the only existing binding, hs-onnxruntime-capi 0.1.0.0 (2025-07-24), is AGPL-3.0-only with no newer version and no candidates — virally incompatible with a permissive toolkit. Verified supply: ONNX Runtime is MIT (spdx_id "MIT") and v1.29.0 (published 2026-08-12) ships onnxruntime-win-x64-1.29.0.zip, onnxruntime-win-x64-gpu_cuda12-1.29.0.zip, onnxruntime-win-x64-gpu_cuda13-1.29.0.zip, onnxruntime-linux-x64-1.29.0.tgz (+cuda variants) and onnxruntime-osx-arm64-1.29.0.tgz. Net effect: "train in PyTorch/scikit-learn, run in Haskell, on Windows, with GPU, under MIT" — a capability that today literally cannot be obtained. Inference only; no training, no export.

A4. hsds-linalg — CBLAS level-3 plus the LAPACKE drivers (gesv, posv, gels, gesdd, gesvd, syevd, geev, getrf/getri, potrf/potri, geqrf/orgqr, trtrs) resolved at runtime from OpenBLAS through hsds-dyn, operating over Storable buffers. Bind the C interfaces (cblas.h/lapacke.h, which OpenBLAS ships headers for), never Fortran symbols, and never reuse hmatrix's build system (0.20.2 from 2021-03-08, Windows issues #236/#284 open since 2017/2018, INSTALL.md self-declared out of date). TWO MANDATORY CORRECTIONS to the source design: (i) the backend is pinned IMMUTABLY at init and there is no withBackend — pure operations over a swappable global via unsafePerformIO are unsound under laziness and non-deterministic across backends, so any backend-consulting op that is not on an immutable pin lives in IO; (ii) either every exposed driver has a pure-Haskell fallback, or drivers lacking one are documented per-driver as requiring a backend — no blanket "nothing hard-fails" banner over a partial fallback set. Engineering hazards budgeted with named tests: LP64 vs ILP64 (MSYS2 ships both openblas and openblas64; probe openblas_get_config at load, because getting it wrong silently corrupts results above 2^31), symbol-presence drift across reference-BLAS/OpenBLAS/MKL/Accelerate, Windows DLL search path and whether the current OpenBLAS zip bundles libgcc_s_seh-1/libgfortran/libquadmath/libwinpthread (ship them if not), and OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS defaulting to 1 against the GHC RTS scheduler. Every operation cross-checked against SciPy in CI to 1e-10 relative error on random and ill-conditioned inputs.

=== TIER B: UPSTREAM CONTRIBUTIONS (no new packages — PRs into the incumbent) ===
B1. Windows + macOS CI for the dataframe monorepo. Verified absent from BOTH workflow files.
B2. Upgrade dataframe-core's existing TypeError sites to GHC.TypeError.Unsatisfiable with hand-written messages (available column names + "did you mean").
B3. The golden type-error corpus as a build-failing CI gate, contributed to dataframe.
B4. Phase/Role leakage typing (Split 'Train, Pipeline 'Fitted) as a PR to dataframe-learn's DataFrame.ModelSelection.
B5. Generic-derived hyperparameter reflection, ADDITIVE to the existing polymorphic gridSearch :: Int -> Int -> [c] -> (c -> DataFrame -> DataFrame -> Double) -> DataFrame -> GridSearchResult c.
B6. Structured column-level schema-mismatch diffs on CSV ingestion (issue #177), against the existing KnownSchema/schemaEvidence.
B7. Inbound Arrow import donated into dataframe-core once hsds-abi proves it.
B8. IHaskell Hackage release carrying PR #1595's Windows support, plus prebuilt kernel bundles.
B9. Independent db-benchmark verification (issue #115 — upstream's numbers are self-published on a Chromebook).
NOT DONE: the Parquet writer. It is the funded, mentored GSoC 2026 project (issue #181, mentors mchav + adithyaov). Offer review, never competition.

=== TIER C: THE THIN SEAM (one package, deliberately small) ===
C1. hsds — umbrella + HSDS.Doctor + the `hsds` executable. `hsds setup {blas,onnx}` performs checksum-pinned (SHA-256) downloads into a per-user data directory, with a documented offline/air-gapped env-var override AND a "point me at an existing libopenblas/onnxruntime" path so corporate proxies do not make the toolkit unusable, plus third-party license attribution. `hsds doctor` reports exactly which capabilities resolved, which did not, and the single command that fixes each. Frame<->buffer marshalling that HONESTLY reports the copy. EXPLICITLY NOT IN C: a DataFrame, a typed schema layer, an Expr or TExpr, an estimator protocol package, a plotting grammar, a CSV/Parquet reader, a query optimizer, an AD engine, a numeric prelude.

=== CROSS-CUTTING POLICY ===
GHC: floor 9.10.3 (Stackage LTS 24.55, verified current), primary and CI-default 9.12.4 (Stackage nightly 2026-08-16, full HLS 2.14 support, and — decisively — the incumbent's own tested ceiling is 9.12.2, so this is where the ecosystem actually lives), forward-tested 9.14.1 as ALLOWED-TO-FAIL (no Stackage snapshot exists for it, HLS gives it basic support only, 9.14.2 is still only rc1 on downloads.haskell.org, and upstream dataframe cannot build there — so a red 9.14 lane is not a bug the project can fix). default-language: GHC2021 declared explicitly in every stanza, because GHC 10.0 silently defaults unspecified code to GHC2024.
BUILD: cabal is the documented default (83.96% vs Stack's 39.59% in State of Haskell 2025); a stack.yaml is a courtesy. Submit to Stackage nightly early; do not plan around an LTS 25 appearing, since LTS has been frozen on ghc-9.10.3 for a year.
LANGUAGE FEATURES: no LinearTypes, no OverloadedRecordUpdate, no RequiredTypeArguments in public API, no Template Haskell on any required path, no typechecker plugin required to compile any public signature, no dependence on Dependent Haskell.
INSTALLABILITY IS A HARD CONSTRAINT: every package must be cabal-installable from Hackage on a clean Windows box with no MSYS2 pacman step, forever. sparkle died leaving Hackage for a Bazel-only build; inline-r is dying of failing Hackage builds.
GOVERNANCE: MIT (matching dataframe so code moves upstream frictionlessly), two named maintainers per package before any 1.0, explicit stable/unstable split at 1.0, "never fork what we can patch", and a bite-sized-issue board because DataHaskell's own survey found contributors want self-contained tasks and explicitly do not want maintainer roles.
phased_plan_outline: P0 (weeks 1-3) - FALSIFY THE WINDOWS THESIS BEFORE WRITING ANY LIBRARY CODE. Deliverables: (a) a Windows + macOS CI workflow donated to DataHaskell/dataframe as a PR — verified absent from both .github/workflows/ci.yml (runs-on: ubuntu-latest, ghc 9.6.7/9.8.4/9.10.3/9.12.2) and .github/workflows/haskell-ci.yml (runs-on: ubuntu-24.04, container buildpack-deps:jammy, ghc 9.4.8-9.12.2); (b) a local build of the entire stack on Windows 11 — dataframe-core, -operations, -csv, -parquet (note it pulls zstd and zlib, and zstd's default-on `standalone` flag compiles ~24 bundled C files), -learn, -viz — with the result published honestly whether it passes or fails; (c) a one-paragraph Discourse post whose first sentence is 'this is not a new dataframe' and which names the three net-new capabilities; (d) MIT LICENSE, GOVERNANCE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md with a good-first-issue policy, and a README section stating what HSDS is NOT. HARD GATE: if the stack does not build on Windows, or if the CI PR is rejected, the Windows differentiator is dead and the whole plan must be rescoped before a line of library code is written. This phase is deliberately the cheapest possible test of the project's central premise.

P1 (weeks 3-7) - hsds-dyn 0.1 TO HACKAGE, ALONE. ~300 LOC: LoadLibraryW/GetProcAddress with AddDllDirectory called before load under `if os(windows)`, System.Posix.DynamicLinker otherwise, a documented search order (env override -> per-user data dir -> system), a Capability record of FunPtrs via foreign import ccall "dynamic", per-symbol lazy resolution, and a version tag. Ships first because it is the keystone that lets every later native capability exist without a build-time C dependency, and because it is independently useful to hmatrix, duckdb-ffi and IHaskell regardless of whether HSDS continues. Exit: a stranger can dlopen an arbitrary library on Windows/Linux/macOS through it and get a typed FunPtr back.

P2 (weeks 6-12) - hsds-abi 0.1 TO HACKAGE. Arrow C Data Interface + Arrow C Stream Interface in BOTH directions (inbound is the verified ecosystem gap) and DLPack DLManagedTensorVersioned import/export. Vendor the ABI headers into a TEST-ONLY cbits directory; hand-write the Storable instances in Haskell so the shipped library needs no C compiler; add a test-suite C file of _Static_assert(offsetof(...) == N) checks that fails CI on layout drift. Ownership: import -> ForeignPtr with the C release callback as finalizer; borrow -> bracket; export -> release callback via foreign import ccall "wrapper" freeing a StablePtr keep-alive. Conformance: Haskell writes a stream over a pipe and pyarrow validates it, pyarrow writes and Haskell validates, both directions in CI on all three OSes, plus leak assertions under +RTS -s and valgrind on the Linux lane. Immediately offer the inbound half to dataframe-core as a PR — that is the moment the project stops looking like a competitor.

P3 (weeks 10-18) - hsds-onnx 0.1: THE HEADLINE CAPABILITY. Bind the ONNX Runtime C API through OrtGetApiBase() -> struct of function pointers, resolved by hsds-dyn. Env/Session/SessionOptions/RunOptions/MemoryInfo lifecycle under bracket; OrtValue <-> Storable buffer zero-copy both ways via CreateTensorWithDataAsOrtValue; shape/dtype introspection; graceful Maybe when the runtime is absent. `hsds setup onnx` fetches the checksum-pinned official archive (onnxruntime-win-x64-1.29.0.zip / win-x64-gpu_cuda12 / linux-x64 / osx-arm64, from the MIT-licensed v1.29.0 released 2026-08-12). Ship the end-to-end demo as the deliverable: train in scikit-learn, export with skl2onnx, run in Haskell on Windows, assert prediction agreement to 1e-6. This is the phase that makes the project matter — it fills a verified license-shaped hole (hs-onnxruntime-capi is AGPL-3.0-only and frozen at 0.1.0.0 since 2025-07-24) with a capability that works on the owner's platform including GPU.

P4 (weeks 14-20, RUNS IN PARALLEL, ALL UPSTREAM, NO NEW PACKAGES) - THE ERROR-QUALITY AND LEAKAGE PRs. (a) Upgrade dataframe-core's existing TypeError sites (AssertAbsent, AssertPresent, AssertAllPresent, AssertKeyTypesMatch, AssertDisjoint, AssertRealColumn, InnerJoinSchema and friends) to GHC.TypeError.Unsatisfiable with hand-written messages carrying available column names and a 'did you mean' — highest value-per-line item identified anywhere in the corpus. (b) The golden type-error corpus as a build-failing CI gate: ~60 known-bad programs compiled via ghc as a subprocess, normalized, byte-diffed against .golden files, with a hard budget of <=6 lines and the offending symbol on line 1. (c) Phase/Role leakage typing (Split 'Train, Pipeline 'Fitted) as a PR to dataframe-learn's DataFrame.ModelSelection — the one guarantee no library in any language ships. (d) Generic-derived hyperparameter reflection, ADDITIVE to the existing type-safe polymorphic gridSearch, never replacing [c] with string maps. (e) Structured column-level schema-mismatch diffs for CSV ingestion (issue #177) against the existing KnownSchema/schemaEvidence. Every item arrives as a finished, tested PR closing an issue already filed.

P5 (weeks 18-26) - hsds-linalg 0.1. CBLAS level-3 plus the LAPACKE driver set resolved at runtime from OpenBLAS through hsds-dyn, over Storable buffers, binding the C headers and never Fortran symbols. Backend pinned IMMUTABLY at init with no withBackend (pure-over-mutable-global is unsound under laziness and non-deterministic across backends); any op that cannot be on an immutable pin lives in IO. Either every exposed driver has a pure-Haskell fallback or drivers lacking one are documented per-driver as requiring a backend — no blanket 'nothing hard-fails' claim. Named tests for: LP64 vs ILP64 (probe openblas_get_config at load; MSYS2 ships both openblas and openblas64 and getting it wrong silently corrupts results above 2^31), symbol-presence drift across BLAS implementations (resolve lazily per symbol, degrade per operation), the Windows DLL search path and whether the current OpenBLAS zip bundles libgcc_s_seh-1/libgfortran/libquadmath/libwinpthread (ship them if not), and OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS defaulting to 1 against the GHC RTS scheduler. Every operation cross-checked against SciPy in CI to 1e-10 relative error on random and ill-conditioned inputs. A CI-verified Windows OpenBLAS lane is the thing hmatrix has not had since 2017.

P6 (weeks 24-32) - hsds UMBRELLA, DOCTOR, SETUP, DOCS, RELEASE. `hsds doctor` prints exactly which capabilities resolved, which did not, and the single command that fixes each. `hsds setup {blas,onnx}` does checksum-pinned (SHA-256) downloads into a per-user data dir, with an offline/air-gapped env override, a documented 'point me at an existing library' path for corporate proxies, and third-party license attribution. Honest frame<->buffer marshalling that reports the copy (Column has no Storable constructor — verified — so there is no zero-copy path and the API must not pretend there is). Docs: four one-page end-to-end tutorials (ONNX inference on Windows; pyarrow round-trip; DLPack handoff; BLAS-backed solve with the doctor output shown). Measure and publish cold-install wall clock and time-to-first-inference as CI-ENFORCED budgets that fail the build on >20% regression — publish the measured numbers, advertise no absolute promise. Submit every package to Stackage nightly.

P7 (ongoing, gate not a phase) - GOVERNANCE AND STABILITY GATE. No package reaches 1.0 until it has two named maintainers. At 1.0, publish an explicit stable/unstable module split (Polars' 2024-07-01 precedent) and a deprecation policy of one minor release of warning with a six-month minimum. Version stability is a marketing asset; Deedle shipping 4.0.1 through 8.0.0 in two months is what the opposite looks like.

DEFERRED, EXPLICITLY OUT OF THE ABOVE (listed so scope stays honest): a DLPack<->hasktorch bridge (non-Windows only); a flag-gated DuckDB escape hatch for Parquet WRITE, retired the moment the GSoC 2026 pure-Haskell writer lands; C kernels with runtime cpuid dispatch; a Storable column representation contributed into dataframe-core (the real fix for the copy seam, but it is upstream surgery on someone else's core type and is a separate owner decision); a GHC SIMD wrapper library; anything involving autodiff, neural-network training, GPU kernels, WASM/JS, distributed compute, R interop, or a curated library inventory page.
open_questions: THE P0 GATE OUTCOME. If the Windows/macOS CI PR is rejected, or if the dataframe stack simply does not build on Windows 11, the project's only differentiator evaporates. Does the owner then (a) pivot to Linux-first and drop the Windows claim, (b) maintain a Windows-compatibility fork despite the 'never fork what we can patch' rule, (c) narrow to the three capability packages that do not depend on the incumbent at all (hsds-dyn, hsds-abi, hsds-onnx), or (d) stop? This must be decided BEFORE P0 runs, not after, so the answer is not made under sunk-cost pressure.

RELATIONSHIP TO DATAHASKELL. Does HSDS live as an independent repo, or does the owner seek DataHaskell org membership? This changes naming, licensing posture, governance, release authority, and whether Tier B contributions are 'donations' or 'internal work'. It also changes the failure mode: inside the org, a stalled maintainer blocks you; outside, you are a second effort in a ~110-person community. I cannot make this call because it depends on whether the owner wants to be a contributor or a principal.

PACKAGE NAMING AND PREFIX. The repo is HSDS. Options: hsds-* (matches the repo, but the acronym is opaque and reads like 'Haskell Data Science' which overclaims relative to the reduced scope); a distinct product name; or names that read as DataHaskell components. Related sub-decision: should hsds-onnx and hsds-dyn carry the project prefix at all, given that both are independently useful to people who will never touch the rest and would arguably see more adoption under neutral names (e.g. onnxruntime-simple, dynamic-capability).

THE ONNX CEILING. Inference-only is the scoped position and it is defensible ('train where the ecosystem is, run where your types are'). But someone will call the absence of training disqualifying. Does the owner accept inference-only permanently, or is there an eventual intent to support training — which forces a choice between hasktorch (no Windows support at all, ~2GB libtorch) and building an AD engine that all three critiques and the historical evidence say not to build?

THE STORABLE COLUMN QUESTION. Contributing a Storable-backed column representation into dataframe-core is the REAL fix for the copy seam and would unlock genuine zero-copy Arrow export and BLAS for the whole ecosystem, not just for HSDS. But it is upstream surgery on another maintainer's core type, needs his buy-in, and is a materially different project from the four capability packages. Is the owner willing to spend months on upstream core-type surgery with no HSDS-branded artifact at the end?

BUDGET AND HEADCOUNT. The reduced plan is roughly 32 weeks of focused part-time work for one to two people, and even that assumes the P4 upstream PRs run in parallel rather than serially. Is that the actual available budget? If the real budget is closer to 12 weeks, the correct cut is P0 + P1 + P3 (Windows CI, hsds-dyn, hsds-onnx) and nothing else — which is still a genuine, shippable contribution.

THE SUCCESS METRIC. The honest metric for this plan is 'these four packages get depended on by people who are not the author, and the upstream PRs land' — NOT 'Haskell has a numpy/pandas/sklearn stack'. The latter substantially exists and belongs to someone else. Calibration point: the incumbent has 261 stars but only 4 Hackage reverse dependencies after 2.5 years and 1,267 commits, three of which are its own author's. Does the owner accept a success definition measured in single-digit external dependents and landed PRs?

LICENSE. MIT (matching dataframe, so code moves upstream frictionlessly and the ONNX/Arrow work can be absorbed without relicensing friction) versus BSD-3 versus Apache-2.0 (which adds an explicit patent grant that matters more for FFI bindings to a Microsoft-owned runtime). I recommend MIT for the upstream-mobility reason, but the patent-grant trade-off is a genuine owner call.

IHASKELL MAINTENANCE LABOR. Cutting a Hackage release of IHaskell that carries PR #1595's Windows support is the single highest-leverage unblock in the onboarding chain, but it is pure upstream maintenance work on a project the owner does not control and produces no HSDS artifact. Is the owner willing to spend that time, and to potentially take on IHaskell co-maintenance as a consequence?

TARGET USER VALIDATION. The only empirically verified buyer is 'the Haskell developer with an occasional data task' (14.53% of 1,417 State of Haskell 2025 respondents). The ONNX capability arguably serves a different and unverified user: the Haskell service that needs to run a model trained elsewhere. Should the owner find one design partner running production Haskell who actually needs ONNX inference BEFORE P3 starts, and let their requirements shape it — accepting that if no such partner exists, P3's justification weakens considerably?
